must_identify.item: The new api pods exit because the name redis does not resolve
must_identify.evidence: The api container tries to resolve REDIS_HOST=redis at startup; with ndots:5 the resolver tries redis.shop.svc.cluster.internal, redis.svc.cluster.internal, redis.cluster.internal, then bare redis — all fail — producing: redis connection failed (attempt 1/5): [Errno -2] Name does not resolve ... The process then calls sys.exit(1)

must_identify.item: The cause is the pod's dnsPolicy None / dnsConfig search domains (cluster.internal), not REDIS_HOST, the redis Service or CoreDNS
must_identify.evidence: But the search domain suffix is wrong: it uses cluster.internal instead of the cluster's actual domain cluster.local. Because dnsPolicy: None disables all default cluster DNS config ... the pod relies only on this dnsConfig ... Redis itself is healthy and unrelated ... This is purely a DNS-resolution break introduced by the new pod spec, not a Redis outage.

notes: The RCA does not explicitly say REDIS_HOST is fine. It does treat the value 'redis' as correct, notes the nameserver IP matches kube-dns, and says CoreDNS serves cluster.local, which implicitly clears CoreDNS. The proposed fixes (remove dnsConfig, correct the search domains, or rollout undo) all match the acceptable fixes.

reviewer_ai.reason: The answer correctly identifies that dnsPolicy None with search domains under cluster.internal (not cluster.local) causes 'redis' to fail resolution, explicitly clears REDIS_HOST/Redis/CoreDNS ('Redis itself is healthy and unrelated... purely a DNS-resolution break'), and proposes an acceptable fix (revert dnsConfig/dnsPolicy or fix search domains to cluster.local), matching all must_identify items with no wrong answers asserted.

reviewer_2.reason: Both items are stated explicitly: name resolution failure with exit 1, and dnsPolicy None plus cluster.internal search domains as the cause with Redis and the nameserver cleared. Fix (remove dnsConfig, fix to cluster.local, or rollout undo) is acceptable.
